{{DISPLAYTITLE:A<sub>∞</sub>-operad}}
In mathematics, an '''A<sub>∞</sub>-operad''' is a type of [[operad]] used in [[algebraic topology]] and [[homotopy theory]] to describe algebraic structures where the property of [[associativity]] is loosened. In a simple associative operation, such as the multiplication of numbers, the order of operations does not matter: <math>(a \times b) \times c = a \times (b \times c)</math>. An algebraic structure governed by an A<sub>∞</sub>-operad is one where this equality is not strict, but the two sides are connected by a [[homotopy]] (a continuous path or transformation). The operad itself provides the formal structure for these paths and for higher-level paths that ensure all possible ways of regrouping are compatible with each other.

More formally, an A<sub>∞</sub>-operad is a parameter space for a multiplication map that is [[homotopy|homotopy coherently]] [[associative]]. The "A" stands for "associative", and the infinity symbol "∞" indicates that the associativity holds up to an infinite hierarchy of higher homotopies. This concept is fundamental to the study of [[loop space]]s and is a key tool in fields like [[symplectic geometry]] (through the [[Fukaya category]]). (An operad that describes a multiplication that is both homotopy coherently associative and homotopy coherently commutative is called an [[E-infinity operad|E<sub>∞</sub>-operad]].)

== Definition ==
In the (usual) setting of operads with an action of the symmetric group on topological spaces, an operad ''A'' is said to be an ''A''<sub>∞</sub>-operad if all of its spaces ''A''(''n'') are Σ<sub>''n''</sub>-[[equivariant]]ly [[homotopy equivalent]] to the discrete spaces Σ<sub>''n''</sub> (the [[symmetric group]]) with its multiplication action (where ''n'' ∈ '''N'''). In the setting of non-Σ operads (also termed nonsymmetric operads, operads without permutation), an operad ''A'' is ''A''<sub>∞</sub> if all of its spaces ''A''(''n'') are contractible.  In other [[category (mathematics)|categories]] than topological spaces, the notions of ''homotopy'' and ''contractibility'' have to be replaced by suitable analogs, such as [[quasi-isomorphism|homology equivalences]] in the category of [[chain complex]]es.

== ''A''<sub>''n''</sub>-operads ==
The letter ''A'' in the terminology stands for "associative", and the infinity symbols says that associativity is required up to "all" higher homotopies. More generally, there is a weaker notion of '''''A''<sub>''n''</sub>-operad''' (''n''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;'''N'''), parametrizing multiplications that are associative only up to a certain level of homotopies. In particular,

* ''A''<sub>1</sub>-spaces are [[pointed space]]s;
* ''A''<sub>2</sub>-spaces are [[H-space]]s with no associativity conditions; and
* ''A''<sub>3</sub>-spaces are homotopy associative H-spaces.

== ''A''<sub>∞</sub>-operads and single loop spaces ==
A space ''X'' is the [[loop space]] of some other space, denoted by ''BX'', if and only if ''X'' is an [[Algebra over an operad|algebra]] over an <math>A_{\infty}</math>-operad and the [[monoid]] ''&pi;''<sub>0</sub>(''X'') of its connected components is a group. An algebra over an <math>A_{\infty}</math>-operad is referred to as an '''<math>\mathbf{A}_{\infty}</math>-space'''. There are three consequences of this characterization of loop spaces. First, a loop space is an <math>A_{\infty}</math>-space. Second, a connected <math>A_{\infty}</math>-space ''X'' is a loop space. Third, the [[group completion]] of a possibly disconnected <math>A_{\infty}</math>-space is a loop space.

The importance of <math>A_{\infty}</math>-operads in [[homotopy theory]] stems from this relationship between algebras over <math>A_{\infty}</math>-operads and loop spaces.

== ''A''<sub>∞</sub>-algebras==
An algebra over the <math>A_{\infty}</math>-operad is called an <math>A_{\infty}</math>-algebra. Examples feature the [[Fukaya category]] of a symplectic manifold, when it can be defined (see also [[pseudoholomorphic curve]]).

== Examples ==
The most obvious, if not particularly useful, example of an <math>A_{\infty}</math>-operad is the ''associative operad'' ''a'' given by <math>a(n) = \Sigma_n</math>. This operad describes strictly associative multiplications. By definition, any other <math>A_{\infty}</math>-operad has a map to ''a'' which is a homotopy equivalence.

A geometric example of an A<sub>∞</sub>-operad is given by the Stasheff polytopes or [[associahedron|associahedra]].

A less combinatorial example is the '''operad of little intervals''': The space <math>A(n)</math> consists of all embeddings of ''n'' disjoint [[interval (mathematics)|intervals]] into the unit interval.
